oracle.description: templates/dispatch/tests/test_release_scorecard_cli.py decides correctness: the I/O shell that makes a scorecard producible by running one command. The tolerant-parse fixtures are the load-bearing half -- the sink is appended to by a shell hook on every assistant turn, so one truncated line from an interrupted write must not cost a release its whole scorecard.

purpose: Add four functions to templates/dispatch/scripts/release_scorecard.py -- load_sink_rows, load_receipts, filter_by_window and main -- and change nothing already in it. load_sink_rows(path) reads a JSON-lines file and returns the parsed dicts. It is deliberately tolerant: blank lines, lines that are not valid JSON, and lines that parse to something other than a dict are all skipped rather than fatal, and a path that does not exist returns an empty list. That tolerance is the point, not laxness -- the sink is appended to by a shell hook on every assistant turn, so one truncated line from an interrupted write must not cost a release its whole scorecard. load_receipts(root) parses every <task>/receipt.json beneath root and returns them sorted by task_id, so a scorecard is reproducible instead of filesystem-order dependent; a subdirectory without a receipt, an unparseable receipt, and a missing root are all skipped or empty rather than errors. filter_by_window(records, start, end, key) keeps the records whose key timestamp falls in the half-open window from start inclusive to end exclusive, comparing ISO-8601 strings directly, which is correct for the fixed-width UTC format the sink writes. A None bound means that side is unbounded. A record missing the key, or carrying a non-string there, is excluded: a record that cannot be placed in time cannot be attributed to a release. main(argv) takes --release, --sink, --receipts and --out, with optional --since and --until bounding the window (sink rows filtered on ts, receipts on recorded_at) and an optional --escalations JSON-lines file whose absence means an empty list rather than an error. It builds the scorecard with build_scorecard and writes it to --out as JSON with indent 2 and a trailing newline, creating the parent directory if it is missing, and returns 0. It must not invent its own aggregation: the written file must equal build_scorecard called directly on the same loaded inputs, because a CLI that re-totals its own way is how two paths drift apart. Nothing here shells out to git or resolves tags -- the window is given, not discovered. Leave no debugging output behind.
required_outcomes: a malformed sink line is skipped, never fatal
receipts are returned sorted by task_id, not in filesystem order
the window is half-open: inclusive at start, exclusive at end
a record that cannot be placed in time is excluded
main writes exactly what build_scorecard returns, with no aggregation of its own
a missing --escalations means an empty list, not an error
nothing already in the module changes and no debugging output is left behind

acceptance_properties.requirement: one bad line does not cost a release its scorecard
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a truncated, blank, or non-object line raises instead of being skipped, or a missing path raises

acceptance_properties.requirement: the window boundary does not double-count
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a record exactly at end is kept, a None bound is treated as a real bound, or an untimestamped record is included

acceptance_properties.requirement: the CLI is a shell, not a second implementation
acceptance_properties.fails_when: the written file differs from build_scorecard called directly on the same inputs, or the output is not indent-2 JSON with a trailing newline

non_goals: the six functions already in the module, which are settled
git tag resolution -- the window is given, not discovered
any change to the scorecard's shape, which build_scorecard owns
